Definition: probably from the alternate of G2064; unrestrained (to go at pleasure), i.e. (as a citizen) not a slave (whether freeborn or manumitted), or (genitive case) exempt (from obligation or liability):--free (man, woman), at liberty.
BiblicalUsage: eleútheros is a plain word for free, at liberty. In Matthew 17:26, the text says "Then are the children free." In John 8:33, the text says "and were never in bondage to any man."
TheologicalSignificance: Reading eleútheros this way, I believe freedom in Christ is real freedom: not doing whatever we please, but being set free to live as God made us to live. That is why I keep this word in mind when I read those passages — it carries more than its size suggests.
